recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed in the current FHIR source unless a separate work-group decision asks to alter historical release snapshots or revise the OID regex again.
issue_request: FHIR-16023 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core datatype issue asking to reconcile the OID regex shown on datatypes.html with the oid.value regex in profiles-types.xml. The approved resolution was to use [0-2](\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*))+.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by git-svn commit 8f4b0e6555542518ecbc96bafa30e32eaa3b364d, 'GF#16023 - fix oid regex', corresponding to SVN revision 14079. That commit changed source/datatypes.html and source/datatypes/primitives.xml to the approved OID regex.
additional_context: Current source/datatypes.html uses the [%regex oid%] placeholder, while source/datatypes/primitives.xml contains the current authoritative regex urn:oid:[0-2](\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*))+. Current release4, release4b, and release5 history snapshots contain the corrected generated profiles-types regex. The old profiles-types regex remains only in release2 and release3 historical snapshots, which are not current source inputs to edit. Confluence MnM minutes corroborate the 2018 Persuasive with Mod block-vote disposition, and community searches found no conflicting rationale.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative datatype source and the narrative placeholder already implement the approved FHIR-16023 resolution; editing historical release snapshots would not be a current-spec correction.
